ownership_note: This package is scoped to the single entry 0x007d9410 and to the two instructions the committed listing holds for it. The other bodies the wider neighbourhood package reconstructs (0x007d93a0, 0x007d9420, and the internals of the tail target 0x007d9bb0) are outside this package's evidence pack and are NOT reconstructed here: 0x007d9bb0 is declared as an external callee with the contract the JMP fixes and is defined as an observer in the model test, so nothing about its internals is claimed. mechanics.body_shape: an adjustor thunk of two instructions: reduce the entry register by four, then transfer control to 0x007d9bb0 unconditionally. No prologue, no frame, no saved register, no memory operand of any kind, no comparison, no branch
mechanics.entry_register_rewind: 0x007d9410 SUB ECX,0x4. The four is the entire content of the body. It is applied unconditionally -- the listing holds no conditional branch, so a null entry register is rewound like any other value and the transfer still happens, delivering 0xfffffffc on a 32-bit machine. The model reproduces the wraparound through std::uintptr_t rather than C++ pointer arithmetic, because subtracting from a pointer that may sit anywhere in the address space is undefined behaviour in the source language while SUB on a 32-bit register is not
mechanics.transfer: 0x007d9413 JMP 0x007d9bb0 -- direct, unconditional, and the last instruction in the body. abi_derived.tail_call records {present: true, form: 'jmp', target: '0x007d9bb0', after_frame_setup: false}
mechanics.stack_neutrality: the body contains no PUSH, no POP, no ADD ESP and no SUB ESP, so the caller's one argument word is still where the caller pushed it when the target runs, and nothing this body does can be seen by the target other than the entry register
mechanics.no_field_access: the complete two-instruction listing names no memory operand through any register, so the body addresses no object and writes nothing. Verified in the model test by byte-comparing a receiver block across seven entry offsets
mechanics.argument_identity: deliberately unnamed. The SDK/Ghidra prototype stored on the symbol declares two stack slots, (int virtualKey, KeyModifiers modifiers), while the machine drops exactly one word. Nothing in this pack says which declared parameter that word is, so the model types it as a plain Word and the conflict is carried below
mechanics.globals: none: the complete two-instruction listing names no data-segment address
mechanics.control_flow: no conditional branch at all, which is the evidence that the body is straight-line and that its single transfer is reached for every input

return_semantics.value: whatever the tail target leaves in the return register, forwarded without interpretation. Because the JMP is the last instruction, there is no instruction in this body that could change it
return_semantics.why_not_bool: The persisted ABI record and the SDK/Ghidra prototype both declare bool at the declaration site, and the machine in fact returns a pointer-shaped word, so a caller reading the slot sees a non-zero value. But this body executes no comparison and writes no register other than ECX: it has no opportunity to produce, normalise or reject a boolean, and the derived record for it names no return register at all. Declaring bool in the source would require inserting a `!= 0` that no instruction in the listing performs, so the model forwards the word under the derived record's own classification language instead. The model test pins this down with result words that are neither 0 nor 1 (0xdeadbeef, 0x80000000, 0x7fffffff, 0xffffffff), which a normalising reconstruction cannot reproduce.
return_semantics.ownership: Nothing is claimed. The forwarded word is whatever the tail target produces, and no record for this target or for 0x007d9bb0 in this pack establishes whether it is owned, borrowed, a handle or a plain pointer.
return_semantics.lifetime: The body acquires and releases nothing. It performs address arithmetic on the entry register and transfers control; whatever lifetime the forwarded word has is established, if at all, by the tail target, which this package does not reconstruct.
return_semantics.validator_cost: This choice is the sole reason RETURN SEMANTICS reports WARN instead of PASS. The WARN is correct and was accepted rather than bought back: see validation.expected below.

unresolved_questions: Ordinary-argument arity and identity. The SDK/Ghidra prototype stored on this symbol declares two four-byte stack slots, (int virtualKey, KeyModifiers modifiers), while the machine shows one word being dropped by the tail target's RET 0x4. The model implements the single machine-observed word and types it as an opaque Word. Whether a preceding virtualKey argument exists in the original source and is simply unconsumed, and which declared parameter this word is, is not established by anything in this pack.

Whether the forwarded word is a bool. The declaration site says bool; the body cannot produce one. If a caller really does test the slot as a boolean, the observable truth is that the machine always returns a non-zero pointer-shaped word -- but nothing here establishes that any caller observes it as false, and this model does not claim it does.

What the entry register points at. The persisted ABI record calls it a subobject of cMouseCamera that the body rewinds to the object start; the derived record declines to call ECX a receiver at all, because the body only ever writes it. The two readings are compatible with the two instructions and neither is established by them.

What 0x007d9bb0 does. Its body is outside this package's evidence. Read live during this session it calls 0x007d93a0, tests bit 0 of the caller's argument, conditionally calls 0x00f47380 with the receiver, and returns the receiver in EAX -- but none of that is claimed here, and the record for 0x007d9bb0 is not in this repository's index for this VA.

The class and interface identities behind the three associated vtable words 0x007d93a0, 0x01412890 and 0x01412894, and the meaning of the single data-segment xref at 0x01412894. The binary carries no MSVC RTTI and the word at 0x014128a8 is not a code address in this image.

Whether the two staged packages for this VA (this one and reconstruction/staging/pkg-app-mouse-camera-keydown/) should be merged or kept apart. They agree on every machine fact about the two instructions; they differ in scope (this one reconstructs the entry alone, the other reconstructs a wider neighbourhood) and in the return-type choice recorded under return_semantics. Reconciling them is an integrator decision and was not attempted here.

conditions: The original process is driven to a state where the OnKeyDown slot at 0x01412894 is called, so the entry register and the caller's argument word have real values.

The value of the entry register is captured on entry and the value the tail target receives is captured at its entry, so that the four-byte rewind is confirmed on a real object rather than only on the listing.

The value left in the return register when control returns to the original caller is captured, so that the forwarded word can be compared against both the unclassified model and the declaration-site bool.
The number of return addresses on the stack at the tail target's entry is observed, which is the only way to confirm from the running process that this entry is a tail transfer rather than a call.

expected_reasons.ABI: WARN, and it is a property of the evidence rather than of the source. The derived envelope records conventions.confidence UNKNOWN, and validate.py's arm order reaches its ABI_UNKNOWN and UNKNOWN-confidence branches before it ever asks whether the source declared a convention. Nothing a source file can say moves this check. The source does declare __thiscall and the validator does read it (PKG_DFW_007D9410_THISCALL resolves to thiscall through the package header), and the source is not what the check is complaining about.
expected_reasons.CALLS: PASS. Two independent machine sources agree: the xref export records the single out-edge 0x007d9413 -> 0x007d9bb0, and the complete two-instruction listing shows exactly one direct transfer, JMP 0x007d9bb0, which DIRECT_TRANSFER reads as a transfer because it counts JMP as well as CALL. The span names the same one address (tail_transfer_target_007d9bb0) and no other, and _intra_procedural_jump_targets filters nothing because the jump target lies outside the body span 0x007d9410..0x007d9417.
expected_reasons.GLOBALS: PASS. The complete listing names no data-segment address and the span's code names none either. The source's hexadecimal literals all sit in comments, which _code strips before the token scan, so the span declares no data address to disagree with.
expected_reasons.FIELDS/OFFSETS: PASS, by the receiver-agnostic absence arm. The derived receiver record names no register (register null, offsets []), so there is no register to scan the listing under; the parse record consumed the body in full (declared_count 2, degraded false, unparsed 0) and the listing has no bracketed memory operand and no implicit-memory mnemonic, so the body addresses no object at all. The span declares no member access and no displacement literal -- the four is written in decimal, deliberately -- so there is no offset to ground.
expected_reasons.CONSTANTS: PASS. The listing is fully parsed (2 of 2, 0 unparsed) and the span's code contains no 0x literal at all, which is the 'states no hexadecimal constant' arm. Every hex token in this package's source lives inside a comment and is stripped before the scan.
expected_reasons.CONTROL FLOW: PASS. The complete listing contains no conditional branch, which is itself the evidence that the body is straight-line. The span also happens to contain none of if/for/while/switch, though keyword shape is explicitly not part of this verdict.
expected_reasons.VIRTUAL DISPATCH: PASS. The complete body names no indirect transfer through a register or a memory operand, the derived dispatch record agrees at indirect_calls 0, and the span declares no slot boundary (no load_slot, object_slot, shell_slot, vtable or slot[ token in its code).
expected_reasons.RETURN SEMANTICS: WARN, by deliberate choice. The bounded ABI record claims return_type bool; the model returns unclassified_in_EAX because the body executes no comparison and cannot produce a boolean. The check compares the two strings and warns on any difference. Declaring bool in the source would have bought this PASS and required inserting a `!= 0` that appears in no instruction of the listing, so the WARN was accepted. This is the single check in this package that a different, less careful reconstruction would have made green.
expected_reasons.EVIDENCE COVERAGE: WARN, and it is not reachable from this package. 11 of 17 static evidence categories are available; the pack reports unavailable/MISSING for callees_dependencies, callers_dependencies, contradictions, external_callees, globals, runtime and semantic_hypotheses. The check is derived purely from the pack's category availabilities, so no source or sidecar edit can move it.
expected_reasons.RUNTIME: GATED at 0. No original-process trace exists in this repository. Nothing was attempted and nothing failed; this is an open capability gate, not a per-target finding.

observed.how_measured: The validator was re-run read-only (write=False) with validate._source monkeypatched to resolve to reconstruction/staging/pkg-dfw-007d9410/dfw_007d9410.cpp, because the shipped resolution path cannot reach this package (see known_blockers). Nothing in the repository was written by that run; the evidence directory was byte-compared before and after and is unchanged. The verdicts above are that run's output, not an estimate.
observed.coverage_ratio_if_reported: 6 of 8 structural checks PASS (0.75); with EVIDENCE COVERAGE counted, 6 of 9 (0.667)

known_blockers: Static aggregate is WARN, so tools/reconstruction_tooling/promote.py will refuse this target (REQUIRED_STATIC_STATUS is PASS and the aggregate requires all eight structural checks to be PASS). Two checks are responsible, and neither is closable from this package: ABI WARN is the derived record's own UNKNOWN confidence, and EVIDENCE COVERAGE WARN is the pack's 11-of-17 category availability. The third non-PASS, RETURN SEMANTICS, is a modelling choice this worker made on purpose and would reverse the moment the source declared a return type the machine does not produce.

Tooling, reported and not fixed: validate.py resolves a target's source from reconstruction/knowledge/index.json's record.source.files, a list built once per VA by the index builder. This VA already had a registered source, so the list still names reconstruction/staging/pkg-app-mouse-camera-keydown/mouse_camera_on_key_down_007d9410.cpp and _source() returns that file. A second, newly staged package for the same VA is therefore invisible to the validator: its CALLS, GLOBALS, FIELDS/OFFSETS, CONSTANTS, CONTROL FLOW, VIRTUAL DISPATCH and RETURN SEMANTICS arms are all adjudicated against the older package's text. The verdict in reconstruction/evidence/007d9410/validation.json (which shows RETURN SEMANTICS PASS) describes the older package and says nothing about this one. Re-indexing would repoint the list, but which package wins is an integrator decision, not a worker's.

Tooling, reported and not fixed: validate.py's _abi_category() reads only categories['abi'], while the machine-derived sub-records and the conflicts array this pack actually carries live in categories['abi_derived'] (_machine_record reads abi_derived first, and the pack's own code comment says the envelope layer is where those facts usually are). So _abi_conflicts() is handed None for this pack and the unresolved conflicts entry -- {field: calling_convention, kind: inferred_vs_persisted, resolution_status: unresolved} -- is never seen, which is why the ABI check lands on its UNKNOWN-confidence WARN rather than on its unresolved-conflict FAIL. Measured across the committed packs: 254 carry the inference envelope in categories.abi, 95 in categories.abi_derived, and 9 of those 95 carry a non-empty conflicts array that the ABI check's FAIL arm can never read. This target is one of the 9.

Not a blocker, recorded so it is not mistaken for one: the validator's RETURN SEMANTICS check compares the source's return-type token against the persisted record's string. 'unclassified_in_EAX' and 'bool' are both legitimate positions for this body; the check treats disagreement as needing review and has no way to know which side is wrong. It warned, and the WARN is the correct output for the source as written.

model_test.style: plain int main() with explicit checks; no gtest, no framework, no external dependency
model_test.observer: tail_transfer_target_007d9bb0 is defined in the test as a recording observer, so the test both sees the transfer and chooses its return word
asserted: entering four bytes into a block hands the target the block itself
the entry register reaches the target four bytes lower, for seven different entry values
a null entry register still transfers, and delivers 0xfffffffc (the 32-bit wraparound)
an entry value of 0x00000002 delivers 0xfffffffe, not a value above 2^32
the caller's argument word crosses the transfer unchanged for seven different words, on the null path too
the tail target's return word comes back verbatim, including 0xdeadbeef, 0x80000000, 0x7fffffff and 0xffffffff
no byte of a receiver block is written, for seven different entry offsets
sixteen invocations make exactly sixteen transfers, none skipped and none doubled
model_test.known_limit: A store that wrote back the value it had just read would leave the receiver bytes identical and pass the no-write check. Such a store is not observable through this interface and is not claimed to be excluded; every store that changes a byte is excluded. The claim that the body performs no memory access comes from the listing, not from this test.
